exposure: Single-shot spinal anesthesia (SSSA) with 2.5-mg hypobaric bupivacaine alone
SSSA with 2.5-mg hypobaric bupivacaine and 10-mg fentanyl
SSSA with 2.5-mg hypobaric bupivacaine and 0.5-mg morphine
outcome: Duration of the second phase of delivery
cohort: Ninety healthy multiparous parturients in the active phase of progressing labor (cervical dilatation >=7 cm; pain score >4) requesting analgesia.
finding: The addition of fentanyl or high-dose morphine to bupivacaine increases the efficacy and duration of single-shot spinal anesthesia in the active phase of labor without increasing side effects.
gest_age: 38.7 ± 1.5 weeks (interpreted from stated 'months' given the context of human labor)
